newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Court drops suit against Russian insurer sale.
newsitem.headline: Court drops suit against Russian insurer sale.

text.p: The Moscow Arbitration Court has dropped a suit from a union of depositors in state-owned Sberbank and other securities holders on the legality of OAO Rosgosstrakh's privatisation, company president Vladislav Reznik said on Tuesday.
"The court did not take the suit into consideration as it could not understand what kind of organisation the plaintiff was, or what authority it has," Vladislav Reznik told Reuters.

The union had filed suit against Russia's privatisation ministry, the State Property Committee, saying Rosgosstrakh's privatisation was illegal as the scheme did not include a way of repaying huge sums owed to the clients Rosgosstrakh had before economic reforms started in 1992.
According to different estimates, Rosgosstrakh owes between 30 and 24 billion roubles at 1992 prices (up to $300 million at exchange rates early in the year).
In 1996 President Boris Yeltsin issued a decree converting Rosgosstrakh's debt into state debt, but no concrete ways of implementing the decree have been worked out.
Reznik said any decision taken by the court would not have affected his company's privatisation.
"You cannot reverse what has already been done," he said.
Under the Rosgosstrakh privatisation scheme, 20 percent of its shares were sold to employees and a management team has a priority right over 30 percent.
The remaining 50 percent will be sold at a cash auction this year.
